title: Server proxy routes ignore the configured bridge host and auth token
body:
## Summary
The `/api/pof-bridge/*` proxy calls 127.0.0.1 with no auth header, while the client connects to the configured host with X-Pof-Auth-Token.

## Description
src/lib/pof-bridge/proxy.ts:93 fetches `http://${POF_BRIDGE.HOST}:${port}/pof/...` and src/lib/pof-bridge/proxy.ts:95 sends only Content-Type. src/lib/pof-bridge/client.ts:64 sends the token and src/hooks/usePofBridge.ts:79 passes the configured host and token. With a token set, the connection reads connected while every proxied route answers 401 ("auth token missing or wrong" from src/lib/pof-bridge/proxy.ts:131, a token the server has no way to obtain since it lives in browser localStorage). A non-loopback host is reached by the client and not by the proxy.

## Flow
- set pofAuthToken and a plugin that enforces it
- usePofBridge connects and shows connected
- GET /api/pof-bridge/manifest answers 401

## Expected impact
Anyone running a secured or remote bridge gets a connected badge over broken features. Could break callers that rely on the loopback default if the plumbing changes it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - proxy and client reach the same plugin the same way
Before: proxy sends 0 auth headers and 1 fixed host; client sends the token and the configured host (read in code)
After: not built
Method: simulation - walked the two code paths; no plugin enforcing a token is reachable in a round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
instrument: Fake plugin that returns 401 without X-Pof-Auth-Token, driving a proxy route with a configured token; assert 200 after threading the token/host server-side.

title: PoF Bridge auth token persisted in plain localStorage
body:
## Summary
The bridge auth token is persisted in plain localStorage by pofBridgeStore.

## Description
src/stores/pofBridgeStore.ts:95 includes pofAuthToken in the persist partialize, so the credential sits in the pof-bridge localStorage key readable by any script in the origin. The registry credential-vault / browser-credential-boundary subjects put credentials server-side.

## Flow
- set a token in project setup
- localStorage["pof-bridge"] contains it in clear

## Expected impact
Removes a browser-readable credential; moving it changes where the setting lives, which is a storage decision for the operator.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - credential not readable from browser storage
Before: 1 credential in plain localStorage (read in code)
After: not built
Method: simulation - moving the token server-side is a design choice the round cannot make
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture

title: autoDetect and autoSyncLiveState cannot be changed by anything
body:
## Summary
Two persisted bridge settings have no writer in the app, so they are constants that look like settings.

## Description
setAutoDetect (src/stores/pofBridgeStore.ts:76) and setAutoSyncLiveState (src/stores/ue5BridgeStore.ts:103) each have 0 call sites outside their store (grep over src, tests excluded). autoDetect is read at src/hooks/usePofBridge.ts:30 and is fixed true, so the bridge always auto-connects. autoSyncLiveState is read once and fixed false.

## Flow
- grep setAutoDetect / setAutoSyncLiveState over src
- 0 callers outside the stores

## Expected impact
The operator either gets a toggle or loses two dead settings; which one is a product call.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - settings the UI offers are changeable
Before: 0 writers for 2 persisted settings (grep)
After: not built
Method: probe - grep count; the choice between adding UI and deleting is not measurable
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
grep -rlw setAutoDetect src (0 outside stores)
grep -rlw setAutoSyncLiveState src (0 outside stores)
src/hooks/usePofBridge.ts:30

title: Editing the bridge port during a failed connect keeps retrying the old port
body:
## Summary
usePofBridge auto-connects only from status disconnected, so a port or host edit while status is error or reconnecting does not retarget the retries.

## Description
src/hooks/usePofBridge.ts:78 gates the auto-connect on `current.status === "disconnected"`. After a failed connect the manager sits in error/reconnecting and src/lib/pof-bridge/connection-manager.ts retries through its existing client, so the new port is used only once someone clicks connect. With three mounted hook instances (AppShell, NewHome, ExportPanel) an unguarded effect would fire three connects, which is why this needs a real design rather than a one-line change.

## Flow
- bridge on the wrong port, status error
- change the port in project setup
- retries continue against the old port

## Expected impact
A corrected port takes effect without a manual reconnect. Could cause connect storms across the three mounts if done naively.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a settings change retargets the connection
Before: simulation: 1 case walked, retries stay on the old port
After: not built
Method: simulation - a hook test against the singleton with three mounts is the rung above
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: renderHook test with a mocked pofBridgeConnection at status error: change pofPort, assert exactly one connect with the new port across three mounts.

title: Rebuild is documented as identical but drops additionalArgs
body:
## Summary
The build route header promises a rebuild re-runs the identical request; additionalArgs are never persisted, so a rebuild omits them.

## Description
src/app/api/ue5-bridge/build/route.ts:5 says "its identical request", while src/lib/ue5-bridge/build-pipeline.ts:567 records that additionalArgs are not persisted and the rebuild runs without them. No in-tree caller sends additionalArgs today (grep: the route only), so the gap is latent.

## Flow
- start a build with additionalArgs
- rebuild it
- the second run omits the args

## Expected impact
A rebuild stops silently differing from the build it repeats, or the docstring stops promising it. No current caller is affected.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - rebuild equals the recorded build
Before: simulation: 1 case; additionalArgs lost
After: not built
Method: simulation - needs a column added to headless_builds and an in-tree caller to matter
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
instrument: Build-rebuild round-trip test with additionalArgs through the real headless_builds row.

title: verify/visual sends any readable file to the provider labelled image/png
body:
## Summary
The route base64-encodes whatever file screenshotPath names and sends it as image/png with no signature check.

## Description
src/app/api/verify/visual/route.ts reads screenshotPath and passes `mime: "image/png"` unconditionally; callers name PNGs (src/lib/prompts/visual-check.ts:105) but nothing checks. A PNG magic-byte check rejects a non-image path before it leaves the machine. Two existing test fixtures use fake bytes and would need real headers, and the unguarded-route question is already carded by quality-evaluation-api.

## Flow
- POST screenshotPath pointing at a text file
- bytes are sent to the vision provider as image/png

## Expected impact
Only real PNGs reach a paid provider. Could break a caller that posts a JPEG today, which is why its callers need checking.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only images are sent to the provider
Before: 0 signature checks before the upload (read in code)
After: not built
Method: simulation - the fix changes two fixtures in other contexts and the caller set needs a sweep
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: Route test with a text file path asserting recognize is not called, plus a caller grep for non-PNG screenshot sources.
